run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T06:00:40Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy's RequestErrorRate was driven by a short 5xx burst on frontend's checkout path that coincides exactly with the replacement of the only payment pod. The payment Deployment was rolled out at 05:51:02Z (new ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 whose pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:51:02Z; the previous ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 was scaled to 0 and its pod killed at 05:51:05Z). The replacement container started at 05:51:05Z but payment's own log shows its gRPC server only started on port 8080 at 05:52:20Z. In that gap checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client spans errored, frontend's POST /api/checkout spans errored, and frontend-proxy's ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans errored, pushing frontend-proxy's 5-minute span error ratio from a 0.00018-0.00094 baseline to a 0.025 peak (the alert annotation reports 0.0222). Payment itself recorded no error spans and logged successful charges once its server was listening, so the failure is checkout's inability to reach payment during the rollout, not a payment application error. The alert fired at 06:00:40Z, several minutes after the burst; metric staleness (data_as_of 3-7 minutes behind observation time in this run) is a hypothesis for that delay. A ConfigMap flag paymentUnreachable is currently 'on' and is kept as an unverified alternative candidate because its value at incident time cannot be read and errors stopped while it still reads 'on'.

claims.text: The frontend-proxy span error ratio sum(rate(ERROR[5m]))/sum(rate(all spans[5m])) was 0.00018-0.00094 from the 05:00:40Z sample through 05:51:40Z, rose to 0.010805 at 05:52:40Z, peaked at 0.025312 / 0.025337 / 0.025050 at the 05:53:40Z / 05:54:40Z / 05:55:40Z samples, then fell to 0.000365 at 05:57:40Z.

Over 05:00:40Z-06:14:10Z frontend-proxy recorded 89.2 ERROR spans on operation 'ingress' and 69.9 ERROR spans on operation 'router frontend egress', against 26232.5 and 26248.7 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans on those same operations.

Per-minute error-span increases for frontend-proxy 'ingress' were 58 in the minute ending 05:52:00Z, 80 in the minute ending 05:53:00Z and 2 in the minute ending 05:54:00Z, and 0 in the surrounding minutes; 'router frontend egress' showed the same concentration (58 and 80 in those two minutes, 0 afterwards).

frontend's ERROR spans over the window are confined to the checkout path: POST /api/checkout 69.9, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 69.9, POST 69.9 and client call grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 69.9, while GET /api/data, GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, cart and ad gRPC calls had 0 error spans.

frontend-proxy's egress error count (69.9 on 'router frontend egress') equals frontend's /api/checkout and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder error-span counts (69.9), consistent with the proxy's failed responses being frontend's failed checkout requests.

checkout's ERROR spans over the window are oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (42.41) and its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (42.46); in the 05:50:00Z-06:00:00Z view checkout's other operations (HTTP POST, orders publish, CartService/GetCart, CartService/EmptyCart, CurrencyService/Convert, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart) carried only STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

The payment service's own spans show STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 0 for every span name over the window (charge, grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, dns.lookup, tcp.connect, GET), while its 'charge' span rate fell from about 0.65-0.72/s before the burst to 0.30-0.446/s at the 05:53:00Z-05:57:00Z samples.

The payment Deployment has two ReplicaSets: revision 1 payment-55766d76b9 (replicas 0, created 2026-11-17T05:18:50Z) and revision 2 payment-54499f9786 (replicas 1, created 2026-11-17T05:51:02Z), both with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, identical env and resources and no readiness/liveness/startup probes; the revision-2 pod template alone carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:51:02Z.

Kubernetes events record the old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 'Killing' at 2026-11-17T05:51:05Z and the new pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started between 05:51:02Z and 05:51:05Z, with Deployment payment scaling ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1 and payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0.

The replacement payment container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 2026-11-17T05:52:20.571Z, its first 'Charge request received.' at 05:52:53.971Z, and thereafter 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs through 05:57:58Z and again at 06:04:59Z.

Deployment payment in namespace otel-demo applied the change that produced the burst: its rollout restart at 05:51:02Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) removed the only payment pod at 05:51:05Z, the replacement's payment gRPC server only started listening at 05:52:20Z, and the errors occurred inside that interval - checkout's PaymentService/Charge errors, frontend's /api/checkout errors and frontend-proxy's ingress/egress errors were concentrated in the minutes ending 05:52:00Z-05:54:00Z and were zero afterwards.

frontend-proxy ingress span throughput was 21.1-24.5 spans/s throughout the 05:47:00Z-06:06:00Z samples, including 22.9, 22.5 and 23.2 spans/s at the samples spanning the error burst, so the error-ratio rise was not a request-volume spike.

Per-minute error-span increases between 05:51:00Z and 05:56:00Z were non-zero only for frontend (224 in the minute ending 05:52:00Z, 328 in the minute ending 05:53:00Z), frontend-proxy (116, 160, 2) and checkout (146.5), apart from 2 fraud-detection errors and 2 recommendation errors outside the burst; accounting, ad and payment showed 0 in every bucket.

At query time every otel-demo pod, including payment-54499f9786-4r25d (started 05:51:02Z), frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt and checkout-5dccddf8bb-h9bvp, was Running with ready=true and 0 restarts; Service payment selects opentelemetry.io/name=payment on port 8080 and Endpoints payment has address 100.96.5.201.

No Evicted, OOMKilled, Failed or BackOff reason appears in the events read for otel-demo (only Normal Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/Killing/ScalingReplicaSet events from the payment rollout), and no otel-demo pod shows a non-ready container or restart count.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config, read at about 06:17Z, declares flag paymentUnreachable with defaultVariant 'on' (description 'Payment service is unavailable') while every other flag in that ConfigMap has defaultVariant 'off'.

Payment application errors are not the source of the burst: payment's own spans carry no ERROR status and payment's log records only successful 'Transaction complete.' charges for the requests it received from 05:52:53Z onward, so checkout's failed Charge spans reflect calls that did not reach a working payment backend.

Against the paymentUnreachable setting being the active fault during the burst: error spans stopped after the minute ending 05:54:00Z and payment completed charges again at 06:04:59Z, while the ConfigMap read at 06:17Z still declares paymentUnreachable 'on'; a currently-'on' flag therefore does not by itself match the observed, time-bounded failures.

Payment returning failed charges (paymentFailure flag or an application-level charge failure in payment) is rejected as the cause: the paymentFailure flag defaults to 'off' in flagd-config, payment's spans show 0 ERROR, and payment's log records only successful transactions during the burst window.

The alert timestamp 06:00:40Z, about six minutes after the error burst ended, may reflect telemetry pipeline lag: this run's metric views returned last samples several minutes before observation time (data_as_of 06:10:40Z while observed 06:17:17Z, freshness 187-423 s), so an evaluation at 06:00:40Z could still have been reading the 05:52-05:54 burst whose 5-minute error ratio (up to 0.0253) is close to the annotated 0.0222.

ConfigMap flagd-config's paymentUnreachable flag ('on' at 06:17Z, description 'Payment service is unavailable') remains an unverified alternative candidate: a flag-driven checkout-side payment-unreachable injection would produce the same symptom (checkout PaymentService/Charge errors without payment-side errors), but its value during 05:51-05:54Z cannot be read and errors stopped while it still reads 'on'.

Because the frontend-proxy error ratio stayed non-zero after the burst (about 0.0007 in the 5-minute-ratio samples from 05:57:40Z to 06:10:40Z, from scattered 2-4 error spans per few minutes), a rule whose condition is simply 'error rate above 0' could keep firing after the checkout burst; the alert rule named RequestErrorRate was not retrievable, so this cannot be confirmed.

Give the single-replica payment Deployment a readiness/startup probe and a rollout strategy (or a second replica) so a pod-template change does not remove payment from the Service endpoints before the process is listening; the observed gap was 05:51:05Z to 05:52:20Z with no readiness probe configured.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, so what issued the Deployment payment rollout restart (the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation at 05:51:02Z) and who changed it could not be read.

The value of ConfigMap flagd-config during 05:51-05:54Z is unknown: the ConfigMap was read only at query time, its edit history is not available, and the flagd pod (flagd-678dcfdc67-bl78w) log read returned no data, so whether paymentUnreachable was 'on' during the burst cannot be verified.
The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate was not found by name in the rule listing (that query returned no_data), so the rule's exact expression, threshold and evaluation window are unknown.

Jaeger trace searches for frontend-proxy (05:55-06:17Z) and checkout (05:50-06:17Z) returned no_data, and a wider checkout search over the full window hit RESULT_TOO_LARGE, so span-level error messages, gRPC status codes and parent-child references for the failing Charge calls could not be inspected.

The checkout container's filtered log read for 05:51:30Z-05:58:00Z returned no_data after excluding 'payment went through', and the frontend container log read returned no_data, so the exact client-side failure text was not observed.
The deleted payment pod's logs (payment-55766d76b9-846r8) are no longer available, so its shutdown/termination behaviour and the exact connection-refused error text cannot be read.

An instant query for kube_deployment_status_replicas_available/ready of deployment payment at 06:17:09Z returned no_data, so deployment replica status from kube-state-metrics could not be confirmed; pod phase/ready state came from the Kubernetes API instead.
Metric data ended at data_as_of 06:10:40Z, so the interval 06:10:40Z-06:17:09Z is unobserved.
next_steps: Review the Kubernetes audit/change log for a 'kubectl rollout restart' or patch of deployment/payment in namespace otel-demo at 2026-11-17T05:51:02Z to identify who triggered it.

Verify the effective flag set served by flagd (via the flagd UI/API and its config history) to determine whether paymentUnreachable was 'on' during 05:51-05:54Z, and reconcile it with the observed successful charges.
Inspect the alerting rule behind RequestErrorRate and its evaluation lag to confirm it was reading the 05:52-05:54Z burst rather than a later residual error rate.
Add readiness/startup probes and surge or a second replica for the payment Deployment before any future rollouts.
